findings.title: Shard sub-requests are interpolated a second time, with request.filters applied again
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() already calls applyTemplateVariables on every target (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52). Each shard sub-request is then passed to runSplitQuery(), which calls applyTemplateVariables again on the already-interpolated targets, and passes the same request.filters. The updated shard test confirms this: it now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for one target (1 from the shard entry point plus 4 sub-requests). The PR's goal is to interpolate once at the start, but the change repeats the work for every sub-request. Interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: any value that contains a '$' token after the first pass gets substituted again, and ad-hoc filter handling that appends matchers would run once per sub-request. Fix by interpolating in only one place, for example by having the shard path call an internal runner that skips interpolation.

findings.title: $__range check now runs on the interpolated expression, so $__range queries can be split
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() uses isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to stop queries that use $__range from being split. The comment says $__range must reach the backend so it is computed over the split time range. With this PR, runSplitQuery interpolates each query with applyTemplateVariables (line 299) before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting. If request.scopedVars contains __range, the token is already replaced when the check runs, so the check no longer matches. The query is then split, and each chunk is computed over the whole range's value of $__range, so the merged result differs from the unsplit query. The new test only covers $__auto and $step, so nothing catches this. Fix by checking the range variable on the raw expression before interpolation, and update the comment, which becomes misleading.

findings.title: Empty-expression filter now runs before interpolation, so variables resolving to empty are sent
findings.body: The filter on query.expr used to run after interpolation, so a target whose expression was a variable resolving to an empty string was dropped. It now runs on the raw expression, before the map that interpolates it. A target such as '$query' whose value is empty is kept, and an empty expression is sent to Loki, which returns a parse error that shows up in the panel. Previously that target was silently skipped. Filter again after interpolation, or keep the previous order.

findings.title: Test asserts the redundant interpolation count instead of guarding against it
findings.body: The test now expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times for a single target. That count encodes the double interpolation of shard sub-requests (one call in runShardSplitQuery plus one per runSplitQuery sub-request), so the test locks in the behavior the PR should avoid. No test checks that each target is interpolated exactly once, and none checks that request.filters is applied once. Those assertions are needed once the double interpolation is fixed.
